segments.text: Welcome to Real Easy English from BBC Learning English.

segments.text: In this programme, we have real conversations in easy English

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: to help you practise listening and learn new words and phrases.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: I'm Beth.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And I'm Neil.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: In each episode, we talk in English about a different topic

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: that you need for everyday speaking.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: If you want to read along, you can visit our website,

segments.speaker: Neil

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Hello Beth.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Hi Neil, how are you?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I'm very well, thank you.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: What are we talking about today?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, today's episode is all about family.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We'll be talking about who is in our families

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: and comparing them.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, great.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So, what do we mean when we say comparing our families, Beth?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, when we compare two things, we look at them and see if they are the same or different.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And we can compare things in different ways, but we often do it with adjectives.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK, let's start the conversation.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So, Neil, how big is your family?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It probably average really I have one sister but she has three kids and I have two kids

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: So when we get together with my parents, there are a few of us. It's not tiny. It's not huge.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Okay. Yeah. I think my family is definitely smaller than yours because I don't have any

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: brothers or sisters. I am an only child. So when I get together with my family, it's very small

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: because I also only have one cousin and she is an only child as well. So my family's tiny.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Okay. And what is your family like? It's small, but what's it like?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: It is small, but we're very close. So we see each other quite often. We are a bit silly.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We like to go out and have food and play games and we can be quite loud even though there aren't many of us.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: OK. It sounds like you get on well with your family. Is that right?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Yeah, definitely. Yeah. I love spending time with my cousin and she has two children.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: What about you? Do you get on well with your sister?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, I get on well with my sister.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: We don see each other very often because we don live in the same place But when we see each other we have a nice time We catch up and chat So Beth we have used the expression get on well with someone What does that mean

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Well, that means that you have a good relationship with them. So, if you get on well with your

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: sister, it means when you're together, you're happy, you're not fighting. It's easy to have

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: good conversation. You don't really have any arguments. Maybe when you were a child, you

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: didn't get on well with your sister. I don't know.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Yes, I think now that we are grown-ups, it's easier to get on well with your sibling. When

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: I was a kid, maybe I was a bit mean to her.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Oh dear. So Neil, your sister has three children. What are the ages of them?

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Well, for a start, they're all boys.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Okay. Oh my gosh, that sounds very difficult.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And the oldest one is 17.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And he has just done his driving test.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: It's difficult to believe because he's the oldest.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: He's always been the oldest, but now he's almost an adult.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: And is he the oldest, including your children?

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: So out of all the kids, he's the oldest.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: He is, yeah.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: so in my family

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: my cousin has two children and they are five and two

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: little ones

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: yeah they are the youngest in the family but i was the youngest in my family until they came along and i am 32 so

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: i was used to being the youngest but i'm not the youngest anymore now we've got little ones

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: oh well

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: are you sad

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: no i'm okay

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: OK,

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: let's quickly recap the vocabulary we learned in this conversation.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: We learned compare, which means to look at two things to see if they are the same or different.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: Bigger and smaller, which are ways to compare the size of something.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Youngest and oldest, which are ways to talk about the age of someone or something.

segments.speaker: Neil
segments.text: And we looked at get on well with someone, which means to have a good relationship with them.

segments.speaker: Beth
segments.text: Thanks for listening to Real Easy English.
